#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
We now use a host local exec instead of SSH commands to simplify the test and make the result more robust.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Follow-up of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/101866

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
None

comments:
I got annoyed that I couldn't click through to see the other logs, so now you can, ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/22923

(spyglass doesn't render build-log.txt because it's 500MB, and the limit for rendering is 100MB)

/assign @wojtek-t @mm4tt @shyamjvs 
SIG Scalability chairs/TLs, please find someone to address or call this a non-release-blocking failure

This is sig-node issue - should be addres by SIG-node folks.

/sig node
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/103640 is being discussed as a fix for this and I'm not sure it's correct
@wojtek-t is it sig scalability's intent that 5k node clusters should support SSH?

The SSH test in question passes in the "default" job: https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-master-default&include-filter-by-regex=SSH

So the fact that this failure is unique to a scalability job means to me that scalability needs to own at least some part of this

I did a little bit of digging and ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-correctness uses `- --gcp-ssh-proxy-instance-name=gce-scale-cluster-master` option in kubetest, which according to https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/2b77449e7fcaa977b84e979f5544ad1eb6f1c7f8/kubetest/main.go#L90 seems to be setting KUBE_SSH_BASTION env. So I believe this is main difference between our scalability job and "default".
Debugging the test in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/103815 and providing a fix there. The crictl host PR (#103640) is doing something different.

review_comments: Not commenting on the removals but the line above.  Is there some less-tied-to-cluster/-way of knowing whether `crictl` is available?
(crictl doesn't seem like a cloud-provider implementation detail)
Hm, how would we do that? Could we say every node should have `crictl` configured? (tending to no)

Honestly if crictl can't reasonably be expected to exist by default on all clusters, this should be tagged with [Feature:CrictlInstalled] or something. I'll leave it be since this is how this has always been, but we should reconsider this for v1.23 or if we ever want to untangle from kube-up.sh
it used to skip the test if there are no ready ssh-able nodes, with this change it will fail. Is it intentional? (PR introduced test skipping: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/101866)

This new combination of `GetBoundedReadySchedulableNodes()` and `hostExec.Execute()` creates a pod on the specific node and run the specified command in the pod without using ssh.
This pr requires just schedulable nodes, and I think it is good that the test fails if there is not such nodes on the environment.

Is there a relation of `gce,gke`and `crictl` or just the CI combination?
I think that this will run now everywhere where the binary is available, i.e., it will run on kind jobs too, 

TODO to skip if binary doesn't exist and not skip by cloud provider
